claims.text: Existing hallucination detection approaches based on self-consistency cannot effectively identify question-level hallucinations.
Existing hallucination detection approaches based on self-consistency cannot effectively identify model-level hallucinations.
SAC3 incorporates semantically equivalent question perturbation and cross-model response consistency checking to detect both question-level and model-level hallucinations.
SAC3 outperforms the state of the art in detecting non-factual statements across multiple question-answering and open-domain generation benchmarks.
SAC3 outperforms the state of the art in detecting factual statements across multiple question-answering and open-domain generation benchmarks.

evidence.description: Re-examination of existing detection approaches uncovered two types of hallucinations resulting from question-level and model-level which cannot be effectively identified through self-consistency check alone.

methodologies.name: Semantic-aware cross-check consistency (SAC3)
methodologies.description: A sampling-based hallucination detection method incorporating semantically equivalent question perturbation and cross-model response consistency checking.
